answer: A sybil farm would need to acquire one opal per fake identity plus pass live proof-of-location, making each clone cost as much as a real node. Each agent stakes a unique opal token bound to a verified hardware root, and every epoch the network samples a random river of attestations that must trace to distinct physical devices. The fable that identities are free collapses once staking and sampling align, so attackers pay linearly for every additional voice. In practice, sa0014 sees clones fail at the grading gate.
